spec.upstream: LADDERDROPWHERE-*.json (E186 month rows), + EDGEDEPTH-*.json (E197) for the k_stop cross-read only
spec.method: for each flagged (era, drop) and each E197 depth k, remove k random months drawn from the pair's own decision months 200 times and record how often the reversal survives; the edge trim's own outcome at that k is read against that null
spec.rng: random.Random(zlib.crc32('era|name|k|seed')) -- a stable per-cell seed, because string hashing is not stable across runs; seed=20261029
spec.units: reversal is a boolean; rates are fractions of draws

class_rules.a_random_removal_of_the_same_size_kills_: the edge kill is not about the months -- any k months do it
class_rules.the_edge_months_kill_where_random_remova: the edge set is doing something the removal count does not
class_rules.random_removal_of_the_same_size_also_usu: the edge survival is not about the months either
class_rules.most_random_removals_of_the_same_size_st: the edge survives where most random removals do not
class_rules.no_null_at_this_depth: too few months left for a reading
class_rules.no_base_reversal: nothing to test on this pair

spec.null_size_note: the null is removal-count-matched to the edge trim at the same k, so a match means the depth curve is a statement about how many months went missing, not about which ones

honest: the month rows are read from the published E186 face; a missing face publishes zero pairs rather than an invented removal set

the edge side is recomputed through E197's own _edge_depth_curve, so the two faces cannot quote different k, size or outcome for the same cell; the E197 k_stop is carried as a cross-read field and is never an input to the verdict
the null draws from the pair's whole decision-month pool, so the edge set is one of its own draws -- this is the same experiment at the same size, not a weaker placebo
a cell whose removal would leave fewer than two months for a reading publishes no null at all instead of a rate over an empty sample
the draws are seeded per cell, so the face is reproducible byte for byte; the trial count is published as randomisation_trials and is a randomisation draw, not a strategy trial

matching the null on count does not prove the edge set is uninformative where the null is flat in both directions: a null rate near 1.0 makes the edge survival unremarkable and says nothing about fragility
removing months changes the sample the verdict is computed on; this measures whether the removal set matters, it does not license dropping any month for real
descriptive census only: no gate, no prereg, no trial count
